primary_diagnosis_treated: Metabolic syndrome (including hypertension, obesity, prediabetes, dyslipidaemia risk)

medications.purpose: Control of essential hypertension and renal protection
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends ACE‑I as first‑line for hypertension; also renoprotective in early CKD (NG107)

medications.purpose: Add‑on antihypertensive to achieve BP <140/90 mmHg
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 advises ACE‑I/ARB plus CCB when BP uncontrolled on monotherapy

medications.dose: 20 mg once daily in the evening
medications.purpose: Primary CVD prevention (QRISK ≥10% or metabolic‑syndrome risk)
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181 recommends moderate‑intensity statin for patients with QRISK ≥10% or metabolic syndrome components

medications.dose: 500 mg with evening meal, titrate weekly to 500 mg twice daily, then 850 mg twice daily, target 1500 mg twice daily (max 2 g/day)
medications.purpose: Improve insulin sensitivity in high‑risk prediabetes
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 recommends metformin for high‑risk prediabetes (BMI ≥30, age ≥35, or other risk factors) when eGFR ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m²

medications.dose: 120 mg three times daily with each main meal containing fat
medications.duration: Until 5 % body‑weight loss achieved, then review
medications.purpose: Adjunct weight‑loss therapy when lifestyle alone insufficient
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181 lists orlistat for BMI ≥30 kg/m² (or ≥28 kg/m² with comorbidities) as pharmacologic adjunct

medications.dose: 200 mg (≈65 mg elemental iron) once daily
medications.purpose: Treat iron‑deficiency anaemia after confirming iron studies
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG107 advises oral iron for confirmed iron‑deficiency anaemia

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive blood‑pressure lowering; risk of symptomatic hypotension
interactions_checked.action: Monitor BP after 1–2 weeks; reduce lisinopril dose if hypotension occurs

interactions_checked.interaction: No clinically significant pharmacokinetic interaction; rare myopathy risk if renal impairment
interactions_checked.action: Check CK if muscle symptoms develop; ensure eGFR ≥30

interactions_checked.interaction: None significant; both renally cleared – monitor renal function
interactions_checked.action: Check eGFR before starting metformin and repeat in 2 weeks

interactions_checked.interaction: Potential minor reduction in absorption of lisinopril if taken simultaneously
interactions_checked.action: Take iron at least 2 h apart from lisinopril

contraindications.reason: eGFR unknown; NICE NG28 contraindicates metformin if eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m²
contraindications.alternative: If eGFR <30, use a DPP‑4 inhibitor such as linagliptin (NICE NG28) instead of metformin

contraindications.reason: Renal protective strategy; NSAIDs worsen hypertension and CKD (NG107)
contraindications.alternative: Use paracetamol for pain if needed

contraindications.reason: Can worsen glucose tolerance and dyslipidaemia (CG181 contraindications)
contraindications.alternative: Low‑dose thiazide (e.g., chlortalidone 12.5 mg) only if further BP control needed

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – assumed ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m² for metformin initiation; order renal panel before starting.
Lipid profile not available – assumed dyslipidaemia risk based on metabolic syndrome; obtain fasting lipids to confirm and monitor response.
QRISK score not calculated – assumed ≥10% given age, BMI, hypertension, prediabetes; calculate at next visit.
Smoking status unknown – assess and offer cessation support as per NICE NG136.
Alcohol intake not quantified – counsel to ≤14 units/week and consider referral to alcohol‑reduction service.
Liver function tests not provided – required before starting statin and orlistat; order LFTs.
Pregnancy status unknown – confirm not pregnant and discuss contraception before ACE‑I and statin use.
Allergy history not documented – verify no hypersensitivity to ACE‑I, statins, or iron.
treatment_summary: The patient with metabolic syndrome and isolated diastolic hypertension should continue lisinopril and add amlodipine to achieve target BP, start atorvastatin for primary CVD prevention, and initiate metformin for high‑risk prediabetes (pending eGFR confirmation). Orlistat is offered as a weight‑loss adjunct if lifestyle measures fail, and ferrous sulphate will be used only after confirming iron‑deficiency anaemia. Monitoring includes BP, renal function, lipids, HbA1c, iron studies, and liver enzymes, with reviews at 4–6 weeks after any new drug start and annually thereafter. All recommendations follow NICE CG181, NG136, and NG28.
